name: r4-m11
statement: After stating an answer, the cued Olmo-3 base often fails to emit EOS and keeps writing like pretraining text (an invented follow-up problem, a variant, a reworking that changes the value). Grader v3 scores the last answer marker, so part of the cued base's MATH-500 deficit comes from answers whose first stated answer was right and were then overwritten by a later marker. RL boxes once and stops, so it does not carry this artifact.
scope: Covers Olmo-3-1025-7B with the 3-token opening cue against Olmo-3.1-7B-RL-Zero-Math (plain), MATH-500, T 1.0 / top-p 1.0, cap 16,384, scored with grader v3 or any other last-marker grader. It claims only a minority share of the about 53-problem net gap (roughly 5 to 20 problems), not the whole gap. It does not cover the loop-driven deficit at T 0.6, cap hits that never reach any answer marker, arithmetic, misreading or method errors, grader recall on equivalent expressions (m12), the harder 328 set, or the weight-difference results.

explains.quote: when the model invents and answers a new problem after its real answer
explains.how: This is the mechanism observed directly: a base answer runs past its real answer into an invented problem, and a last-marker grader extracts the invented problem's answer.
Among the RL-only problems, the hand reader saw base answers that reached the gold value and then wrote a different final value, the overwrite this mechanism predicts.
If the base does not stop after an answer and keeps writing non-repetitive pretraining-style text, it can reach the cap without any zlib loop. This explains cap hits that rule A does not flag.

explains.quote: 6 of base's 7 fixes are format repairs
explains.how: A review pass helps the base by restating or repairing which answer ends the text, not by changing the math. That fits a deficit that lives partly in which answer gets extracted.

explains.quote: no J-lens feature predicts a wrong base answer better than length
explains.how: Post-answer continuation adds length specifically to answers that get graded wrong, which is one reason length separates wrong from right base answers so well.

conflicts.quote: that is the only right-to-wrong flip of 114 over 9 cells
conflicts.how: If invented follow-up answers were common, switching graders should have exposed more of them. However, v1 may also read the last line, so a single flip does not bound how often both graders take the later answer.

conflicts.quote: RL's P(stop) is below 0.5 in 16.5 % of 473 answers (base 4.2 %)
conflicts.how: Where the base actually stops, it is confident about stopping. This shows no weak stopping habit, although those positions are selected because the base did stop there.
The hand reader assigned only 2 of 65 RL-only problems to this category, which is fewer than a large artifact would give, unless tail-only labelling missed early right answers.

rival: The strongest rival is that the residual deficit consists of genuine reasoning failures (misreads, slips, wrong methods) plus grader recall on the final line (m12), and that text after the first answer is rare and changes the answer in both directions about equally often. The two are separated by regrading the FIRST answer marker of each stored answer. This theory predicts a net gain in right answers for the base and none for RL, and predicts that discordant first/last pairs are mostly first-right/last-wrong. The rival predicts no net gain and a roughly symmetric split.

predictions.experiment: First-marker regrade of the base's wrong T1 answers: among T1 rows graded wrong by grader v3 on the full text, the fraction whose first answer marker is right.
predictions.recipe: File: s3 r4/base_rl-02/out/T1.jsonl (500 rows, base + cue, T 1.0). For each row, v3_last = grader/rln4_grader_v3.py applied to the full text against gold (recomputed, since the record has no v3 column). First marker = whichever of these starts earliest in text: (a) a line whose left-stripped text begins with 'Answer:', with content = the rest of that line; (b) the first '\boxed{', with content = the brace-balanced contents. first_score = grader v3 applied to the string 'Answer: ' + content against gold. A row with no marker gets first_score 0. Filter: rows with v3_last == 0, cap hits included. Statistic: (rows with first_score == 1) / (rows with v3_last == 0).

predictions.experiment: Direction of first/last disagreement on T1: among rows where the first-marker grade differs from the last-marker grade, the share that are first-right and last-wrong.
predictions.recipe: File: s3 r4/base_rl-02/out/T1.jsonl, all 500 rows, cap hits included. v3_last and first_score are defined exactly as in the previous recipe (first marker = earliest 'Answer:' line or '\boxed{'; no marker gives first_score 0). Discordant rows: first_score != v3_last. Statistic: (discordant rows with first_score == 1) / (discordant rows). If there are no discordant rows, the statistic is undefined and counts as refuted.
predictions.refuted_by: measured below 0.45, or no discordant rows

predictions.experiment: Net first-marker gain for the base on the four Day-1 #3 samples: (first-marker right count minus stored v3 right count) over all attempt-0 rows.
predictions.recipe: File: iterate-runs:abaybektursun-1114-153825-208b/answers.jsonl (base + cue, T 1.0, 4 samples). Filter: attempt == 0 (500 problems x 4 samples = 2,000 rows; missing rows are dropped and the denominator is the number of rows present). v3_last = the stored score_v3. first_score as in the first recipe (earliest 'Answer:' line or '\boxed{' content, graded by grader/rln4_grader_v3.py as 'Answer: ' + content; no marker gives 0; cap hits included). Statistic: (sum of first_score - sum of v3_last) / number of rows.

predictions.experiment: The same net first-marker gain for the RL model on its four Day-1 #3 samples.
predictions.recipe: File: iterate-runs:abaybektursun-1114-183640-e828/answers.jsonl (RL plain, T 1.0, 4 samples). Filter: attempt == 0 (missing rows are dropped and the denominator is the number of rows present). v3_last = the stored score_v3. first_score as in the first recipe (earliest 'Answer:' line or '\boxed{' content, graded by grader/rln4_grader_v3.py as 'Answer: ' + content; no marker gives 0; cap hits included). Statistic: (sum of first_score - sum of v3_last) / number of rows.

predictions.experiment: Wrong rate among base answers that keep going and state a new answer after the first one: among finished T1 answers with more than 300 characters and at least one further marker after the first marker, the fraction graded wrong by v3.
predictions.recipe: File: s3 r4/base_rl-02/out/T1.jsonl. Filter: cap_hit false and at least one marker (first marker defined as in the first recipe). End of first marker: for an 'Answer:' line, the end of that line (or the end of text); for '\boxed{', the position just after its matching closing brace. Keep rows where the text after that end is longer than 300 characters AND contains another 'Answer:' line (a left-stripped line beginning 'Answer:') or another '\boxed{'. Statistic: (kept rows with v3_last == 0) / (kept rows), with v3_last recomputed by grader/rln4_grader_v3.py. If no rows are kept, the statistic is undefined and counts as refuted.
predictions.refuted_by: measured below 0.20, or no kept rows

predictions.experiment: Stopping test at the first answer: cut each stored T1 base answer just after its first answer marker (end of the 'Answer:' line or the closing brace of the first \boxed, including the newline if present), feed prompt + cue + that prefix back to the base, and sample one continuation (T 1.0, top-p 1.0, max 300 new tokens, seed 81,000,000 + i, H100). Do the same for T2 RL answers cut after their first marker, under the RL model with the plain prompt (seed 82,000,000 + i). Measure, over problems that have a marker, the fraction whose continuation has no EOS within the first 50 new tokens. The predicted value is for the base; the theory also requires the RL fraction to be below the base fraction.
predictions.refuted_by: base fraction below 0.06, or the RL fraction at or above the base fraction
